stem: I said to my mother, "I will certainly take you to Bangalore this week."
optA: I told my mother he would certainly take her to Bangalore that week
optB: I told my mother that I would certainly take her to Bangalore that week
optC: I told my mother that she would certainly take her to Bangalore that week
optD: I told to my mother that I would take you to Bangalore that week
solution: Reported speech needs 'told my mother that', backshift of 'will' to 'would', the second-person 'you' becoming 'her', and 'this week' becoming 'that week'. The first-person subject 'I' stays 'I' because the reporter is the speaker. Matches option B.
subject: English

stem: "How long does the journey take" my co-passenger asked me.
optA: My co-passenger asked me how long does the journey take?
optB: I asked my co-passenger how long the journey would take
optC: My co-passenger wanted to know how long the journey would take
optD: My co-passenger asked me how long the journey did take
solution: A reported question drops the interrogative word order and the question mark, so 'does the journey take' becomes 'the journey would take' with a suitable reporting verb. Options A and D keep the auxiliary in question form and B reverses the speaker. Matches option C.
subject: English
reviewNote: Strict backshift of 'does take' is 'took'; the paper's key uses 'would take', which is acceptable since the journey was still ahead at the time of asking, and every other option is ungrammatical or changes the speaker.

stem: "How clever of you to have solved the puzzle so quickly," said the mother.
optA: The mother exclaimed admiringly that it was very clever of him to have solved the puzzle so quickly
optB: The mother expressed that he was so clever to have solved the puzzle quickly
optC: The mother told that he was very clever in solving the puzzle so quickly
optD: The mother exclaimed with joy that he was clever enough to solve the puzzle so quickly
solution: An exclamatory sentence is reported with 'exclaimed' plus 'that', and 'How clever of you' becomes 'that it was very clever of him'. Only option A keeps the exclamatory reporting verb, the correct impersonal structure and the perfect infinitive 'to have solved'. Matches option A.
subject: English

stem: He said he goes for a walk every morning.
optA: He said, "I went for a walk every morning."
optB: He said, "I go for a walk every morning."
optC: He said, "I will go for a walk every morning."
optD: He said, "He goes for a walk every morning."
solution: Turning indirect into direct, the reported clause 'he goes' restores to the speaker's own words in the first person and present tense, since a habitual action was left un-backshifted. Matches option B.
subject: English

stem: I reiterated, "I don't care about the job."
optA: I reiterated I didn't care about the job
optB: I said again and again I didn't care about the job
optC: I reiterated that I did not care about the job
optD: I repeatedly said that I cared about the job
solution: The reporting verb 'reiterated' is kept, the conjunction 'that' is added, and the present 'don't care' backshifts to 'did not care'. Options B and D replace the verb or reverse the meaning. Matches option C.
subject: English
reviewNote: Option A is also grammatical since 'that' is optional, but C is the fuller standard form and is the intended key.

stem: I said to my brother, "Let us go to some hill station for a change."
optA: I suggested to my brother that they should go to some hill station for a change
optB: I suggested to my brother that we should go to some hill station for a change
optC: I suggested to my brother that let us go to some hill station for a change
optD: I suggested to my brother that let them go to some hill station for a change
solution: 'Let us' addressed to a listener is a proposal, reported with 'suggested that ... should'. The speaker includes himself and is doing the reporting, so 'us' becomes 'we', not 'they'. Options C and D wrongly keep 'let'. Matches option B.
subject: English

stem: I wondered how many discoveries went unheeded.
optA: I said, "How many discoveries have gone unheeded?"
optB: I said, "How many discoveries went unheeded?"
optD: I said, "How many discoveries go unheeded?"
solution: Going from indirect to direct, the backshift is undone, so 'went unheeded' returns to the present 'go unheeded', and the question is restored with a question mark. Matches option D.
subject: English

stem: Gopan said to me, "Can you do these sums for me?"
optA: Gopan asked me if I could do those sums for him
optB: Gopan asked me if I can do those sums for him
optC: Gopan asked me if I can do these sums for him
optD: Gopan asked if I could do these sums for him
solution: A yes-no question is reported with 'asked me if', 'can' backshifts to 'could', 'these' becomes 'those' and 'me' becomes 'him'. Only option A applies all four changes. Matches option A.
subject: English

stem: The boss said, "It's time we began planning our work".
optA: The boss said that it was time they had begun planning their work
optB: The boss said that it was time we had begun planning our work
optC: The boss said that it was time they began planning their work
optD: The boss said that it was time we began planning his work
solution: 'It's' backshifts to 'it was' and 'we' plus 'our' shift to 'they' plus 'their' as the reporter is outside the group. The past subjunctive after 'it is time' does not shift further, so 'began' stays 'began'. Matches option C.
subject: English

stem: He said to the judge, "I did not commit this crime."
optA: He told the judge that he did not commit the crime
optB: He told the judge that he had not committed the crime
optC: He told the judge that he had not committed that crime
optD: He told the judge that he had not committed this crime
solution: 'Said to' becomes 'told', the simple past 'did not commit' backshifts to the past perfect 'had not committed', and the demonstrative 'this' becomes 'that'. Matches option C.
subject: English

stem: AGREEMENT
solution: Agreement means harmony or concord of opinion. Its direct opposite is discord, meaning disagreement or lack of harmony; dislocation, turbulence and fragmentation describe physical or social disruption, not disagreement. Matches option B.
subject: English

stem: AGONY
solution: Agony means intense, overwhelming suffering. Ecstasy, meaning overwhelming joy or rapture, is its exact counterpart in both sense and intensity, which pleasure and bliss (milder states) do not match. Matches option D.
subject: English
reviewNote: Bliss and pleasure are also broadly opposite, but the standard paired antonym of agony is ecstasy, which matches its extreme intensity.

stem: RETICENT
solution: Reticent means reserved and unwilling to speak freely. The opposite is communicative, meaning ready and willing to talk; forward means bold or presumptuous, which is a different quality. Matches option D.
subject: English

stem: PRECISE
solution: Precise means exact and clearly defined. Vague, meaning imprecise or loosely stated, is its standard opposite; incorrect concerns truth rather than exactness, and indistinct refers to unclear perception. Matches option B.
subject: English

stem: CANDID
solution: Candid means frank and outspoken, saying exactly what one thinks. Diplomatic is the true opposite, describing guarded, tactful speech that withholds blunt opinion; cunning is the tempting distractor but opposes honesty rather than frankness. Matches option B.
subject: English
reviewNote: CONTESTED KEY - needs a human call. Duplicate of bank row 46b6cb4a-4982-4676-912f-608eb4042e28 (same headword CANDID, same direction), but that row's options are entirely different, so its key could not be transferred and this one is derived. Keyed B (diplomatic) as the opposite of frank/outspoken; A (cunning) is defensible as the opposite of honest, and the bank row's own answer 'Secretive' sits closer to that reading. Kept PRIVATE either way.

stem: APOCRYPHAL
solution: Apocryphal means of doubtful authenticity or probably untrue. Authentic, meaning genuine and of undisputed origin, is its opposite, while dubious, unsubstantiated and fictitious are all near synonyms of the headword. Matches option A.
subject: English

stem: REPEL
solution: Repel means to drive back or push away. Attract, meaning to draw towards oneself, is its direct opposite. Matches option D.
subject: English

stem: APALLING
solution: Appalling means causing shock, dismay or horror. Consoling, meaning comforting and giving relief, is the opposite, whereas shocking, scaring and horrifying all repeat the sense of the headword. Matches option B.
subject: English

stem: JEST
solution: Jest means a joke or playful, light-hearted talk. Gravity, meaning seriousness and solemnity of manner, is its opposite; sport is a synonym, since to speak in sport is to speak in jest. Matches option A.
subject: English

stem: CURTAIL
solution: Curtail means to cut short or reduce in extent. Lengthen, meaning to extend or make longer, is its opposite, while shorten is a synonym of the headword. Matches option A.
subject: English

stem: to blaze a trail
optA: to lead the way as a pioneer
optD: to wear a blazer while running
solution: To blaze a trail means to be the first to do something and so open the way for others to follow. The literal readings about lighting a track or setting a fire are traps built on the word blaze. Matches option A.
subject: English

stem: red-letter day
solution: A red-letter day is a memorable, happy and important occasion, from the old practice of marking feast days in red on calendars. The colour is incidental, so a colourful day is the literal trap. Matches option C.
subject: English
reviewNote: Duplicate of bank row 8dbe4f91-6e65-4ef3-ad72-abc6e590d225; kept PRIVATE to back the printed paper.

stem: have the last laugh
optC: to be victorious at the end of an argument
solution: To have the last laugh is to end up successful or vindicated after seeming to be losing. It is about final victory, not about humour or cheerfulness. Matches option C.
subject: English
reviewNote: Duplicate of bank row 103f0795-0c11-4555-ac57-b6dd0abe51b4; kept PRIVATE to back the printed paper.

stem: turn a deaf ear
solution: To turn a deaf ear is to refuse to listen to a request, complaint or advice, that is, to ignore it. Defy and disobey imply active resistance to an order, whereas the idiom means simply paying no attention. Matches option A.
subject: English

stem: to smell a rat
solution: To smell a rat is to sense that something dishonest or deceitful is going on. The literal bad smell is the obvious trap, and seeing a hidden meaning is too weak because the idiom carries the sense of suspecting foul play. Matches option D.
subject: English

stem: A few days before his death, he made a clean breast of everything.
solution: To make a clean breast of something is to confess it fully and frankly. Taking off his shirt is the literal reading of breast and is the intended trap. Matches option A.
subject: English

stem: I am done for.
solution: To be done for means to be finished, ruined or doomed with no hope of recovery. It has nothing to do with being answered or rewarded. Matches option A.
subject: English

stem: For a healthy and lasting friendship one must be on the level.
solution: To be on the level means to be honest, straightforward and sincere in one's dealings. Equally rich is the literal reading of level as equal standing. Matches option C.
subject: English

stem: The foolish young man soon made ducks and drakes of the vast property his father left him.
solution: To make ducks and drakes of something is to waste it recklessly, from the game of skimming stones across water. Merely spending or distributing misses the sense of foolish waste that the sentence about a foolish young man requires. Matches option A.
subject: English

stem: All his ventures went to the winds.
solution: To go to the winds means to be scattered and lost, so that the ventures came to nothing. Spreading all over and becoming well known are literal readings that reverse the idiom's negative sense. Matches option A.
subject: English

stem: The intention of the writer of this passage is to
optA: warn the readers against conducting interviews
optB: instruct people on the best means of conducting interviews
optC: tell people how to make friends with interviewers
optD: advise people on the use of letters and telephone
solution: The passage is entirely advisory about how interviews should be run: it ranks the modes ("Letter and telephone interviews are less satisfactory"), recommends face-to-face contact, and insists that "Adequate preparation for the interview is a 'must'". That is instruction on the best means of conducting interviews, not a warning or a note on making friends. Matches option B.
subject: English
context: The interview may be conducted by letter and by telephone, as well as in person. Letter and telephone interviews are less satisfactory. Direct contact with an individual and a face-to-face relationship often provide a stimulating situation for both interviewer and interviewee. Personal reaction and interaction aid not only in rapport but also in obtaining nuances and additional information by the reactions which are more fully observed in a face-to-face relationship. Adequate preparation for the interview is a "must". Careful planning saves not only time but also energy of both parties concerned. The interview is used to obtain facts or subjective data such as individual opinions, attitudes, and preferences. Interviews are used to check on questionnaires which may have been used to obtain data, or when a problem being investigated is complex, or when the information needed to solve it cannot be secured easily in any other way. People will often give information orally but will not put it in writing.

stem: According to the author the best way to conduct interviews is
optA: to talk to the interviewees over telephone
optB: to write letters to the interviewees
optC: to observe the interviewees from a distance
optD: to have a direct conversation with the interviewees
solution: The passage says letter and telephone interviews "are less satisfactory" and that "Direct contact with an individual and a face-to-face relationship often provide a stimulating situation for both interviewer and interviewee". So the best way is direct conversation. Matches option D.

stem: If I want to interview someone,
optA: all I need to do is to just drop in and have a talk with the person
optB: I ought to plan and prepare for the interview well in advance
optC: I have to ring up the person and ask him/her all the questions I want to
optD: establishing good rapport with the person will be enough
solution: The passage states plainly that "Adequate preparation for the interview is a 'must'" and that "Careful planning saves not only time but also energy of both parties concerned". Simply dropping in, telephoning, or relying on rapport alone is therefore ruled out. Matches option B.

stem: Face-to-face interaction with the interviewees enables the interviewer to
optA: understand shades of meaning not readily available in written responses
optB: observe the physical stature of the interviewee
optC: listen to the voice of the interviewee directly
optD: compel the interviewees to express their opinions in writing

Nuances are precisely shades of meaning missing from written responses. Matches option A.

stem: The author used 'individual opinions', 'attitudes' and 'preferences' as examples of
optB: abstract philosophical concepts irrelevant to the interview process
optC: psychological properties particular to a given interviewee
optD: likes and dislikes common to interviewers and interviewees
solution: The passage lists them as "subjective data such as individual opinions, attitudes, and preferences", which is the opposite of objective data and rules out option A. Subjective data of this kind are psychological properties belonging to the particular interviewee, not concepts irrelevant to the interview nor tastes shared by both parties. Matches option C.

stem: One who goes to settle in another country
solution: An emigrant is one who leaves his own country and goes to settle in another; the verb "goes" fixes the viewpoint at the country of departure. An immigrant, by contrast, is one who comes into a country to settle there. Matches option D.
subject: English
reviewNote: Immigrant (option A) is defensible if the sentence is read from the receiving country's viewpoint, but the standard one-word substitution for one who goes out to settle in another country is emigrant.

stem: One who hates mankind
solution: A misanthrope is one who hates mankind. A philanthropist loves and helps mankind, and a misogynist hates women specifically, not all humanity. Matches option C.
subject: English

stem: Belonging to all parts of the world
solution: Cosmopolitan means belonging to or representative of all parts of the world. Universal means applying to all cases or all people generally, versatile means many-sided in ability, and secular means non-religious. Matches option C.
subject: English
reviewNote: Universal (option B) is loosely defensible, but the exact one-word substitution for 'belonging to all parts of the world' is cosmopolitan.

stem: One who walks on ropes
solution: A funambulist is a tightrope walker, that is, one who walks on ropes. An acrobat is a gymnast generally, an upholsterer covers furniture, and an aviator flies aircraft. Matches option A.
subject: English

stem: The study of the origin and history of words
solution: Etymology is the study of the origin and history of words. Linguistics is the study of language as a whole, an anthology is a collection of literary pieces, and verbose is an adjective meaning wordy. Matches option B.
subject: English

stem: It is time to take tea.
optA: It was time that tea was taken
optB: It is time for tea to be taken
optC: It is time that tea should be taken
optD: It is time that tea had been taken
solution: The pattern 'It is time to + verb' is turned into the passive as 'It is time that + object + should be + past participle', so 'take tea' becomes 'tea should be taken'. A and D wrongly shift the sentence into the past. Matches option C.
subject: English
reviewNote: B ('It is time for tea to be taken') is grammatically acceptable English, but the standard textbook transformation for the 'It is time to' pattern is the 'that ... should be' clause, so C is keyed.

stem: The members should adhere to all the decisions.
optA: All the decisions should adhere to the members
optB: All the decisions adhered to the members
optC: All the decisions should be adhered to by the members
optD: All should adhere to the decisions of the members
solution: 'Adhere to' is a prepositional verb, so the passive must retain the preposition: 'should be adhered to by the members'. A and D reverse the roles of members and decisions. Matches option C.
subject: English

stem: His subordinates accused him of various offences.
optA: They accused him of various offences
optB: It was accused by his subordinates that he had done various offences
optC: His subordinates accused that he had done various offences
optD: He was accused of various offences by his subordinates
solution: The object 'him' becomes the subject 'He', 'accused' becomes 'was accused', and the doer is carried by 'by his subordinates', with 'of various offences' unchanged. Matches option D.
subject: English

stem: Has someone made all the necessary arrangements ?
optA: Has all the necessary arrangements been made by someone ?
optB: Have the necessary arrangements been all made by someone ?
optC: Have all the necessary arrangements been made by someone ?
optD: All the necessary arrangements have been made by one ?
solution: The plural subject 'all the necessary arrangements' needs 'Have ... been made', and the quantifier must stay before the noun. A uses the singular 'Has' and B misplaces 'all'. Matches option C.
subject: English

stem: We will know the outcome of these experiments after six months.
optA: The outcome of these experiments will be known after six months
optB: The outcome will be known of these experiments after six months
optC: After six months, we will know the outcome of these experiments
optD: These experiments will have a known outcome after six months
solution: The object 'the outcome of these experiments' becomes the subject and 'will know' becomes 'will be known', the agent 'by us' being dropped as understood. B splits the noun phrase and C leaves the sentence active. Matches option A.
subject: English

stem:
1. A bad habit is harmful, none as harmful as smoking.

P. But habit is second nature, smokers remain smokers for life

Q. Besides being expensive, smoking does injury to one's health

R. In the long run he may get something worse-lung cancer

S. A smoker gets nothing but smoke for his money

6. Then why get that bad habit?
solution: Q opens the case against smoking on both counts, expense and health; R extends the health point to lung cancer; P concedes that the habit persists for life; S returns to the worthless bargain and leads straight into 'Then why get that bad habit?'. Derived order Q R P S. Matches option B.
subject: English
reviewNote: Q S R P would read more smoothly, since S introduces 'a smoker' as the antecedent of 'he' in R, but that order is not offered; QRPS is the closest available and keeps the strong S to 6 link.

stem:
1. Phobic reactions are strong, irrational fears of specific objects or situations

P. But there is no objective danger

Q. For example, when a person is extremely fearful of birds, snakes, heights or closed places, the label phobia is applied to the person's fear and avoidance

R. He usually recognizes that his fear is irrational

S. A person suffering from phobic neurosis knows what he is afraid of

6. But he cannot control it.
solution: Q supplies the example the opening definition invites, P adds the contrast that there is no objective danger, S introduces the sufferer who is the antecedent of 'He' in R, and R's admission that the fear is irrational sets up 'But he cannot control it'. Derived order Q P S R. Matches option A.
subject: English

stem:
1. In this life there are no gains without pains,

P. No victory is a real triumph unless the foe is worthy

Q. Life, indeed, would be dull if there were no difficulties

R. Both winner and loser enjoy a game most if it is closely contested to the last

S. Gainers lose their zest if there is no real struggle

6. Whether we like it or not, life is one continuous competition.
solution: Q generalises the opening 'no gains without pains', S applies it to gainers who lose zest without struggle, R illustrates it with a closely contested game, and P's point about a worthy foe leads into 'life is one continuous competition'. Derived order Q S R P. Matches option B.
subject: English

stem:
1. One Botany professor always tried to convince his students that his branch of biology is superior to all the others

P. His most persuasive argument, however, came during a laboratory session

Q. And they don't eat very much

R. Examining the cells of a pear, the professor cut a slice for the microscopic slide and took a bite of the rest of the specimen

S. Plants, he noted never run away or bite

6. "You won't be doing that in a Zoology lab," he said.
solution: S and Q are the professor's routine claims about plants, P then announces that his most persuasive argument came in the laboratory, and R describes the pear-tasting demonstration that his closing remark refers to. Derived order S Q P R. Matches option B.
subject: English

stem:
1. Failure is nothing to be ashamed of for there is hardly any man who has not failed in life, not once but many times.

P. What is important is the way we take our failure

Q. It has been well said that he who never made a mistake never achieved anything of great worth

R. From the little child who tries to stand up to the would-be conqueror who tries to conquer some new territory, everyone has to face failure

S. If we face our failure boldly and resolve to fight again we are sure to achieve victory in the long run

6. Thus failures can prove stepping stones in our march to victory.
solution: R extends the opening claim that everyone fails, Q backs it with the well-known saying about never making a mistake, P pivots to what really matters, and S states the reward of facing failure boldly, leading into 'Thus failures can prove stepping stones'. Derived order R Q P S. Matches option D.
subject: English

stem:
Consider the following statements: Statement I: Most of the big ports in India are situated on western coast of India.
Statement II: Western Coast of India is a submergent coast.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
optA: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
optB: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
optC: Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
optD: Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
solution: Statement I is correct: the west coast carries Deendayal (Kandla), Mumbai, JNPT, Mormugao, New Mangalore and Kochi, and these include India's biggest handling ports. Statement II is also correct: the western coastal plain is a submerged (submergent) coast, narrow and indented, unlike the emergent eastern coast. Because submergence drowns river mouths and creates deep, sheltered natural harbours, Statement II is precisely the reason the big ports cluster on the west, so it is the correct explanation. Matches option A.
subject: Geography
chapter: Indian Geography — Economy, Resources and Transport

stem:
Consider the following pairs:
Desert Continent
1. Kalahari desert : Africa
2. Namib desert : South America
3. Mojave desert : North America How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
solution: Pair 1 is correct: the Kalahari lies in southern Africa across Botswana, Namibia and South Africa. Pair 2 is wrong: the Namib is a coastal desert of south-western Africa along the Atlantic, not South America (the South American cold coastal desert is the Atacama). Pair 3 is correct: the Mojave lies in the south-western United States in North America. Two pairs are correctly matched. Matches option B.
subject: Geography

stem:
Consider the following statements regarding Tsunamis:
1. They are a kind of earthquake having an epicenter below the oceanic waters. 2. The height of the waves is inversely proportional to the depth of the water.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
solution: Statement 1 is incorrect as worded: a tsunami is not a kind of earthquake but a train of long sea waves generated when an earthquake, landslide or volcanic event with its focus below oceanic water displaces the water column. Statement 2 is correct: in the deep open ocean the wave is only a fraction of a metre high and travels fast, while on entering shallow water it slows and piles up into a towering wall, so height varies inversely with depth. Only statement 2 holds. Matches option B.
subject: Geography
chapter: Earth's Structure, Landforms and Geological Time
reviewNote: Statement 1 is the borderline one. NCERT loosely says an earthquake with its epicentre below oceanic water 'generates' a tsunami, and some keys therefore treat statement 1 as correct and mark C. Strictly a tsunami is a sea wave, not an earthquake, so B is the defensible reading. Source-verify if an official key is available.

stem: Which of the following best describes the "Nebular Hypothesis"?
optA: The universe began with a massive explosion, and galaxies are moving farther apart over time
optB: The planets were formed out of a slowly rotating cloud of material surrounding a youthful Sun
optC: The Earth and the other planets were formed directly from the explosion of a star
optD: The Sun and the planets formed from particles created after the Big Bang
solution: The nebular hypothesis of Kant, later revised by Laplace, holds that the planets condensed out of a cloud (nebula) of material associated with a young, slowly rotating Sun. Option A describes the Big Bang or expanding-universe theory and option D confuses that cosmology with planet formation. Option C describes the supernova or explosion-based ideas, not the nebular hypothesis. Matches option B.
subject: Geography
chapter: Earth in Space, Maps and Coordinates

stem:
Consider the following statements with reference to Red and Yellow soil in India:
1. They develop on crystalline igneous rocks in areas of low rainfall.
2. The reddish color of the soil is due to the diffusion of Iron.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
solution: Statement 1 is correct: red and yellow soils develop on crystalline igneous and metamorphic rocks in areas of low rainfall, mainly in the eastern and southern parts of the Deccan plateau, and extend along the piedmont zone of the Western Ghats. Statement 2 is correct: the red tint comes from the wide diffusion of iron in those crystalline and metamorphic rocks, and the same soil looks yellow where the iron occurs in a hydrated form. Both statements are correct. Matches option C.
subject: Geography

stem:
With reference to Koeppen's scheme of climate classification, consider the following pairs:
Type of Climate Associated Region
1. As : West Coast of India
2. E : Jammu and Kashmir
3. Aw : Extreme western Rajasthan
4. Cwg : Gangetic Plains
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
solution: Pair 1 is wrong: the west coast south of Goa is Amw, monsoon with a short dry season, whereas As (monsoon with dry summer) belongs to the Coromandel coast of Tamil Nadu, which gets its rain from the retreating monsoon. Pair 2 is correct: E, the polar type, is assigned to Jammu and Kashmir along with Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand. Pair 3 is wrong: extreme western Rajasthan is BWhw, the hot desert type, while Aw, tropical savannah, covers most of the peninsular plateau south of the Tropic of Cancer. Pair 4 is correct: Cwg, monsoon with dry winter, covers the Ganga plain, eastern Rajasthan, northern Madhya Pradesh and Punjab. Two pairs are correct. Matches option B.

stem:
Which of the following reasons may be attributed to excessive cold in North India during the winter season?
1. Cold winds coming from the Caspian Sea
2. Early-onset of easterly jet streams
3. Continentality of the north Indian region
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
solution: Statement 1 is correct: around late winter, cold winds from the Caspian Sea and Turkmenistan sweep in and bring cold waves with frost and fog over north-western India. Statement 2 is incorrect: the easterly jet stream is a summer feature that develops over the peninsula after the subtropical westerly jet withdraws, so it plays no part in winter cold. Statement 3 is correct: Punjab, Haryana and Rajasthan lie far from the moderating influence of the sea, so continentality gives them very low winter temperatures, reinforced by snowfall in the nearby Himalaya. Statements 1 and 3 hold. Matches option C.
subject: Geography

stem:
"It is a basin with mountains and hills around, where the drainage is towards the center of the basin, and due to gradual deposition of sediments from basin margins, a nearly level plain forms at the center of basin".
The above landform is best described by which of the following?
solution: The description is the textbook definition of a playa: in a desert basin ringed by mountains and hills the drainage converges on the centre, sediment shed from the basin margins accumulates there, and a nearly level plain results, which fills with a shallow lake when water is sufficient and leaves a salt crust on drying. Sand dunes are wind-built mounds, pediments are gently sloping rock-cut surfaces at mountain fronts, and a pediplain is the extensive surface produced when pediments coalesce after prolonged erosion. Matches option A.

stem:
Consider the following statements with reference to Sand Dunes:
1. Barchans are formed in the areas of varying wind speeds
2. The presence of vegetation hinders the process of formation of sand dunes 3. Sand dunes cannot form perpendicular to the direction of wind movement
How many of the statements given above is/are correct?
solution: Statement 1 is incorrect: crescent-shaped barchans, with their horns pointing downwind, form where the wind direction is constant and moderate and the surface over which sand moves is nearly uniform, not where wind speeds vary. Statement 2 is incorrect: vegetation acts as an obstacle that traps drifting sand and helps dunes build up, which is exactly how parabolic dunes form on partly vegetated sandy surfaces. Statement 3 is incorrect: transverse dunes are aligned at right angles to the wind, forming when the wind is constant and the sand source is an elongated feature set across the wind. None of the three statements is correct. Matches option D.

stem:
Consider the following with reference to karst landform:
1. The Karst region has very little surface drainage.
2. Stalactites and stalagmites are both depositional features of karst landform. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
solution: Statement 1 is correct: karst country developed on soluble limestone has very little surface drainage because water sinks quickly through swallow holes, sinkholes and joints and flows as underground streams, leaving dry valleys at the surface. Statement 2 is correct: stalactites hanging from cave roofs and stalagmites rising from cave floors are both depositional forms built by calcium carbonate precipitated from dripping water, and they may join into a pillar. Both statements are correct. Matches option C.

stem:
Consider the following statements regarding soils:
1. The younger soils show similarity with the parent material.
2. Soils in hot tropical regions exhibit shallower profiles.
3. Humus accumulation is a characteristic feature of the soils in the subarctic regions.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
solution: Statement 1 is correct: immature or younger soils retain the texture and mineralogy of the parent rock because pedogenic processes have not yet reworked them. Statement 2 is wrong: high temperature and heavy rainfall in the humid tropics drive intense chemical weathering, so tropical soils have unusually DEEP profiles, while shallow profiles belong to cold and arid regions. Statement 3 is correct: in subarctic and cold temperate regions low temperatures slow bacterial decomposition, so organic matter accumulates as a thick humus layer. Hence only 1 and 3 hold. Matches option B.
subject: Geography
chapter: Earth's Structure, Landforms and Geological Time
reviewNote: Printed stem asks 'how many statements are correct' but the options list statement numbers (1 / 1 and 3 / 1,2 and 3 / None). Read as a statement list, the correct combination 1 and 3 is unambiguously option B.

stem: Which of the following is incorrect:
optA: All natural earthquakes take place in the lithosphere
optD: Density of rocks does not play any role in the reflection and refraction of waves on seismographs
solution: All natural earthquakes originate within the lithosphere, the rigid outer shell about 200 km thick, so A is correct. P waves are longitudinal or compressional and S waves are transverse, so B and C are correct. D is the false statement: seismic waves reflect and refract precisely because they cross materials of differing density, and that change of direction recorded on seismographs is what reveals the layered interior of the earth. Matches option D.

stem:
Consider the following:
1. Subduction occurs during the convergent plate movement.
2. Mid oceanic ridge was formed by the convergent movement.
3. Himalayas are young fold mountains formed by the convergent movement of Eurasian and Indian plate
Which of the above is incorrect?
solution: Statement 1 is correct: at a convergent boundary the denser plate is subducted beneath the lighter one, forming trenches and island arcs. Statement 2 is wrong: mid oceanic ridges are the classic DIVERGENT boundary, where plates move apart and new basaltic crust wells up, so the ridge is a constructive not a convergent feature. Statement 3 is correct: the Himalayas are young fold mountains raised by the continent to continent collision of the Indian and Eurasian plates. Only statement 2 is incorrect. Matches option B.

stem:
Consider the following statements with respect to 'Continental Drift Theory' proposed by Alfred Wegener?
1. In the beginning all the continents formed a single Continental mass called laurasia.
2. The movement responsible for the drifting of the continents was caused by pole fleeing force and tidal force.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
solution: Statement 1 is wrong: Wegener called the single super continent PANGAEA, surrounded by the mega ocean Panthalassa. Laurasia was only the northern fragment that appeared later, after Pangaea broke into Laurasia and Gondwanaland along the Tethys Sea. Statement 2 is correct: Wegener attributed the drift to the pole fleeing force, arising from the rotation and bulge of the earth, together with the tidal force produced by the gravitational pull of the sun and moon. So only statement 2 is correct. Matches option B.

stem:
Consider the following statements:
A. The Cocos Plate is a young oceanic tectonic plate beneath the Pacific Ocean off the west coast of Central America.
B. The Nazca Plate is an oceanic plate in the southeastern Pacific Ocean.
C. The Caribbean Plate is a mostly oceanic tectonic plate underlying Central America and the Caribbean Sea off the northern coast of South America. Choose the correct statement(s):
solution: The Cocos Plate is indeed a small young oceanic plate lying beneath the Pacific off the west coast of Central America, where it subducts under the Caribbean Plate, so A is correct. The Nazca Plate is an oceanic plate of the southeastern Pacific, off the western margin of South America, whose subduction raised the Andes, so B is correct. The Caribbean Plate is a mostly oceanic plate underlying Central America and the Caribbean Sea, bordering the northern coast of South America, so C is correct. All three descriptions are accurate. Matches option D.

stem: Which of the following is not a divergent plate boundary?
optA: the Great Rift Valley of East Africa
solution: The East African Great Rift Valley is a continental divergent zone where the African plate is splitting, and the East Pacific Rise and the Mid Atlantic Ridge are both spreading ridges where new oceanic crust is created. The San Andreas fault is the exception: it is a TRANSFORM boundary along which the Pacific and North American plates slide horizontally past each other, with crust neither created nor destroyed. Hence the San Andreas fault is not divergent. Matches option C.

stem: In the context Of Physical Geography, Prairies are normally associated with which of the following?
solution: Prairies are the temperate grasslands of the interior of North America, stretching across the central United States and the Canadian plains. The equivalent grasslands elsewhere carry different regional names, such as the Pampas in South America, the Veld in South Africa, the Steppes in Eurasia and the Downs in Australia. Antarctica has no grassland at all. Matches option B.

stem:
Consider the following statements
With reference to Coniferous forests: 1.Coniferous forests found in the Siberian climate are the richest source of softwood.
2.Major species of Coniferous forests are pine, fir, spruce, and larch.
3.The leaves of the trees are small, thick, leathery, and needle-shaped.
How many of the above statements are correct?
solution: Statement 1 is correct: the taiga belt of the Siberian type climate is the world's greatest reserve of commercial softwood, supplying pulp, paper and timber. Statement 2 is correct: pine, fir, spruce and larch are the dominant conifers of that belt. Statement 3 is correct: the leaves are small, thick, leathery and needle shaped with a waxy coat, an adaptation that cuts transpiration during the long frozen winter when water is unavailable. All three statements hold. Matches option C.
subject: Geography

stem:
Consider the following statements with reference to Steppe Climate:
1. The steppe type of climate in both the northern and southern hemisphere has extreme winter and summer.
2. The steppe type of climate found in tropical regions of the world.
Which of the statements given above is /are Correct?
solution: Statement 1 is wrong: only the northern hemisphere steppes, lying deep inside the Eurasian and North American landmasses, have truly extreme continental winters and summers. The southern hemisphere temperate grasslands, the Pampas, Veld and Downs, sit on narrow landmasses close to the sea, so the maritime influence keeps their winters mild and the range far smaller. Statement 2 is also wrong: the steppe or temperate continental type is a mid latitude climate of continental interiors, not a tropical one. Neither statement is correct. Matches option D.
subject: Geography
reviewNote: Judged on the standard temperate-continental (Goh Cheng Leong / NCERT) treatment of Steppe climate. Under a strict Koppen reading BSh semi-arid steppe does occur in tropical latitudes such as the Sahel, which would make statement 2 arguable; the NDA convention treats steppe as temperate, so D stands.

stem:
Consider the following statements:
1. The North Sea, in spite of its location in higher latitudes, records higher salinity due to more saline water brought by the North Atlantic Drift.
2. Black Sea records no fresh water influx by rivers.
3. The salinity of water in the depth of oceans depends mainly on evaporation and precipitation. How many of the above are correct?
solution: Statement 1 is correct and is the standard textbook example: despite its high latitude the North Sea has raised salinity because the North Atlantic Drift carries warm saline water into it. Statement 2 is wrong: the Black Sea records very LOW salinity precisely because large rivers such as the Danube pour huge volumes of fresh water into it. Statement 3 is wrong because it misplaces the cause: it is SURFACE salinity that depends mainly on evaporation and precipitation, whereas salinity at depth is largely fixed since no water is added or removed there. Only statement 1 is correct. Matches option A.
subject: Geography
reviewNote: The subtopic list has no dedicated salinity/ocean-water-properties line. Filed under Ocean Currents because the correct statement turns on the North Atlantic Drift; 'Tides and Ocean Movements' is the alternative if the bank files salinity there.

stem: Which of the following is the correct order for lakes moving from North to South?
optA: Lake Victoria, Lake Tanganyika, Lake Malawi and Lake Turkana
optB: Lake Turkana, Lake Victoria, Lake Tanganyika and Lake Malawi
optC: Lake Tanganyika, Lake Victoria, Lake Malawi and Lake Turkana
optD: Lake Turkana, Lake Victoria, Lake Malawi and Lake Tanganyika
solution: Lake Turkana lies farthest north at about 3 degrees N in the Kenya-Ethiopia rift, Lake Victoria straddles the Equator, Lake Tanganyika extends from about 3 to 9 degrees S, and Lake Malawi lies farthest south at about 9 to 14 degrees S. The correct order moving from north to south is therefore Turkana, Victoria, Tanganyika, Malawi. Matches option B.
subject: Geography
subtopic: World — Rivers, Canals and Water Bodies

stem:
Consider the following statements with reference to a particular climatic region:
1. The summer is dry and warm, while there is rainfall in winter.
2. Trees have small broad leaves and are widely spaced leading to the absence of shade.
3. This climate favours viticulture and wine production is an economic activity here.
Which of the following climatic regions best reflects the above-mentioned features?
solution: Dry warm summers with rainfall concentrated in winter is the defining reversed rainfall regime of the Mediterranean or warm temperate western margin climate. Its sclerophyllous vegetation carries small thick leaves on widely spaced trees that cast little shade, and the belt is the world's chief grape growing and wine producing region. Equatorial climate is wet through the year, polar climate is cold and dry, and savanna receives its rain in summer. Matches option D.
subject: Geography

stem:
Consider following statements with reference to the favorable condition for formation of delta:
1. The presence of a large oxbow lake in the river course is one of the favorable conditions for formation of delta.
2. The presence of steep gradients around the delta helps in consolidation of sediments around the delta.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
solution: Statement 1 is wrong, because the ABSENCE of large lakes in the river course is the favourable condition; a lake acts as a settling basin and traps the sediment load that a delta needs. Statement 2 is also wrong, because a gentle gradient with a shallow, sheltered sea is required so that sediment can settle and consolidate, whereas steep gradients keep material in motion and sweep it away. Neither stated condition favours delta formation. Matches option D.
subject: Geography

stem:
Consider the following statements about water vapour content of the atmosphere:
1. It absorbs parts of the insolation from the sun and preserves the earth's radiated heat.
2. Water vapour also contributes to the stability and instability in the air.
3. It accounts for about 4 percent of the atmosphere in tropical regions
How many of the above statements is/are correct?
solution: Water vapour absorbs part of the incoming insolation and also holds back outgoing terrestrial radiation, acting like a blanket that keeps the earth neither too hot nor too cold, so statement 1 is correct. Through the release and absorption of latent heat it alters lapse rates and buoyancy, so it does contribute to stability and instability of the air, and statement 2 is correct. Standard NCERT wording records that water vapour accounts for about 4 per cent of the atmosphere by volume in the warm and wet tropics against less than 1 per cent in dry polar and desert air, so statement 3 is correct as well. All three are correct. Matches option C.
subject: Geography

stem:
With reference to coal deposits in India, consider the following statements: 1. Brown coal is found in coastal areas of Tamil Nadu, Gujarat and Puducherry.
2. About 80 per cent of the coal deposits in India is of bituminous type and a significant portion of it is of non-coking grade.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
solution: Brown coal is lignite, and India's principal lignite reserves lie in the coastal tracts of Neyveli in Tamil Nadu, Kutch in Gujarat and Puducherry, so statement 1 is correct. About 80 per cent of India's coal deposits are of bituminous type and a large share of that is of non-coking grade, which is why coking coal for steel making has to be imported, so statement 2 is correct. Matches option C.

stem: What is the process that tends to build up the land surface by deposition of solid material in its lower areas known as:
solution: Aggradation is the geomorphic process that builds up a land surface by depositing solid material in its lower areas, and it is the counterpart of degradation. Abrasion is the scouring of a surface by rock debris carried in ice, water or wind, attrition is the mutual wearing down of the transported fragments themselves, and agglomeration refers to particles clumping together rather than to any surface building. Matches option C.
subject: Geography

stem: Which one among the following statements about diastrophism is correct?
optA: The forces may be so slow and gradual that they pass unnoticed for a long period of time
optB: The forces may be both slow and sudden that they pass for a short period of time,
optC: The forces may be sudden and so fast that they pass unnoticed for a long period of time
optD: The forces may be slow but for a short period of time
solution: Diastrophism covers the endogenic orogenic and epeirogenic movements that warp, fold, fault and uplift the crust. These forces operate so slowly and gradually that they pass unnoticed for long stretches of human time and become evident only over geological periods. The other options wrongly describe the forces as sudden, or as acting only for a short period. Matches option A.

stem:
Statement I: Volcanic eruption is accompanied by earthquakes.
Statement II: Volcanoes erupt water
vapours and dust particles in the atmosphere. Code:
optA: Both the Statements are individually true and Statement II is the correct explanation of Statement l
optB: Both the Statements are individually true but Statement II is not the correct explanation of Statement l
optC: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
optD: Statement I is false but Statement II is true
solution: Statement I is true, since the rise of magma, gas pressure and collapse of the magma chamber generate volcanic earthquakes before and during an eruption. Statement II is also true, because eruptions throw water vapour, other gases and dust particles into the atmosphere. However the tremors are produced by the mechanical movement of magma and the rupture of rock, not by the ejection of vapour and dust, so Statement II is not the explanation of Statement I. stem: Xeriscaping' is a concept related to:
optB: landscaping related to save soil erosion
solution: Xeriscaping is a landscaping practice for dry and drought prone areas that relies on native drought tolerant plants, mulching, soil improvement and efficient irrigation so that little or no supplementary watering is needed. Its defining aim is conservation of water, not the checking of soil erosion or any process of rock weathering. Matches option A.

stem: Which of the following best describes an esker?
optA: A linear ridge formed by glacial abrasion along valley floors
optB: A sinuous ridge of sorted sediments deposited by meltwater beneath glaciers
optC: A crescent-shaped hill of unsorted glacial till indicating ice direction
optD: A U-shaped valley formed by glacial plucking
solution: An esker is a long sinuous ridge of stratified and sorted sand and gravel laid down by meltwater streams flowing in tunnels within or beneath a glacier, left standing as a ridge once the ice melts away. A drumlin is the crescent or egg shaped hill of unsorted till whose steep stoss end records the direction of ice movement, a U shaped trough is an erosional glacial valley, and a moraine is unsorted debris dumped directly by ice. The sorted, meltwater deposited character is what marks an esker apart. Matches option B.
subject: Geography
chapter: Earth's Structure, Landforms and Geological Time

stem:
Direction of Plate Movements: Plate tectonics studies structural geology and geophysical data rather than sedimentary rock nature to determine plate movements.
Consider the following statements
1. Igneous rocks are rich in natural gas.

2. Igneous rocks are rich in metallic minerals.
3. Igneous rocks are not fossiferous.
4. Igneous rocks consist of silicate minerals.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
solution: Statement 1 is wrong: natural gas, petroleum and coal are hydrocarbons trapped in sedimentary strata, never in igneous rocks. Statement 2 is correct, since igneous rocks are the primary source of most metallic minerals. Statement 3 is correct because fossils are preserved only in sedimentary beds, and cooling magma destroys organic remains. Statement 4 is correct as igneous rocks are formed from magma and lava and are largely made of silicate minerals. So statements 2, 3 and 4 are correct. Matches option C.
subject: Geography

stem:
Which of the following is correct About Potholes and Plunge Pools.
1.Over the rocky beds of hill-streams more or less circular depressions called potholes form because of stream erosion aided by the abrasion of rock fragments. 2.Over the rocky beds of hill-streams more or less circular depressions called Plunge Pools form because of stream erosion aided by the abrasion of rock fragments.
solution: The NCERT text defines potholes exactly as given in statement 1: over the rocky beds of hill-streams, more or less circular depressions form by stream erosion aided by abrasion of rock fragments. Plunge pools are a different, more specific feature, namely very large potholes scoured at the base of a waterfall by the falling water, so statement 2 misapplies the pothole definition. Since the two statements are otherwise word-for-word identical, only one of them can carry the definition, and it belongs to potholes. Statement 1 alone is correct. Matches option A.
subject: Geography
chapter: Earth's Structure, Landforms and Geological Time
reviewNote: The two statements are identical apart from the feature named, so the question turns on one word. A plunge pool is genuinely a kind of very large pothole, but it is defined by its position at the foot of a waterfall, not by the generic hill-stream bed setting given here; hence statement 2 is judged incorrect rather than the pair being jointly true. Not marked flawed because option A remains defensible on the NCERT wording.

stem:
Identify and tick the correct answer
In streams that flow rapidly over steep gradients, normally erosion is concentrated on the bottom of the stream channel. Also, in the case of steep gradient streams, lateral erosion on the sides of the valleys is not much when compared to the streams flowing on low and gentle slopes. Because of active lateral erosion, streams flowing over gentle slopes, develop sinuous or meandering courses. It is common to find meandering courses over floodplains and delta plains where stream gradients are very gentle. But very deep and wide meanders can also be found cut in hard rocks. Such meanders are called:
solution: Meanders that are deeply cut into hard rock, formed when a meandering stream on a gentle gradient is rejuvenated by uplift and cuts vertically downwards while keeping its looping course, are called incised or entrenched meanders. River terraces are stepped bench remnants of former floodplains, alluvial fans are depositional cones at the mountain foot, and deltas are depositional landforms at a river mouth, so none of those fits a meander cut in hard rock. Matches option B.
subject: Geography
chapter: Earth's Structure, Landforms and Geological Time

stem: ______________ is an opening more or less circular at the top and funnel-shapped towards the bottom with sizes varying in area from a few sq. m to a hectare and with depth
solution: The described feature, circular at the top and funnel-shaped towards the bottom, ranging from a few square metres to a hectare in area, is the sinkhole of karst topography, formed by solution of limestone. A swallow hole is the specific opening through which a surface stream disappears underground, a cave mouth is simply the entrance of a cave, and a stalagmite is a depositional column rising from a cave floor. The printed spelling Sinkhokes is an obvious misprint for Sinkholes. Matches option D.

stem: Which one among the following planets has the largest number of known satellites ?
solution: Saturn now holds the largest confirmed satellite family in the solar system, with well over two hundred recognised moons after the batches confirmed from 2023 onwards, ahead of Jupiter at roughly ninety-five. Mars has only two, Phobos and Deimos, and Neptune has about sixteen, so both are far behind. Matches option D.

stem:
Which of the following is correct about the Low Sedimentary Coast.

1.Along low sedimentary coasts the rivers appear to extend their length by building coastal plains and deltas. The coastline appears smooth with occasional incursions of water in the form of lagoons and tidal creeks.

2.When waves break over a gently sloping sedimentary coast, the bottom sediments get churned and move readily building bars, barrier bars, spits and lagoons.
solution: Statement 1 is the standard description of a low sedimentary coast, where rivers prograde the shoreline by building coastal plains and deltas and the coastline stays smooth apart from lagoons and tidal creeks. Statement 2 is also correct, since waves breaking on a gently sloping sediment-rich shore stir the bottom material and rework it into bars, barrier bars, spits and lagoons. Both statements are therefore correct. Matches option C.

stem: Which of the following statements is not correct regarding the motions of the earth?
optA: The sun is vertically overhead at the equator only on two days each year
optB: During equinoxes, all parts of the world have equal days and nights
optC: The Arctic and Antarctic circles mark the limits of the overhead sun
optD: The shortest night in the northern hemisphere falls on the and 21st of June
solution: The limits of the overhead or vertical sun are the Tropic of Cancer at 23.5 degrees North and the Tropic of Capricorn at 23.5 degrees South, not the Arctic and Antarctic circles, which instead mark the limits of the midnight sun and the polar day and night, so statement C is not correct. Statement A is correct because the sun is overhead at the equator only on the two equinoxes, 21 March and 23 September. Statement B is correct as days and nights are equal everywhere at the equinoxes. Statement D is correct since 21 June is the summer solstice in the northern hemisphere, giving its longest day and shortest night. Matches option C.

stem: 'Pingos' are associated with which one of the following processes ?
solution: Pingos are ice-cored, dome-shaped mounds that grow where groundwater freezes and expands beneath the surface in permafrost terrain. They are the classic landform of the periglacial zone, the cold region lying beyond the margin of an ice sheet rather than beneath a glacier itself. They are not produced by moving ice (glacial), by wind (aeolian) or by running water (fluvial). Matches option B.

stem: A region with summer temperature of 20°C, winter temperature of - ° 15 C, annual rainfall of about 50 cm, mainly in spring and early summer and coniferous vegetation would in the:
optA: cold temperature marginal type environment of sri lanka
optC: cold temperature Central or Siberian type environment
solution: A summer of about 20 degrees C against a winter of about minus 15 degrees C gives an annual range of roughly 35 degrees C, which is a strongly continental figure found deep inside a large landmass. Rainfall of only about 50 cm concentrated in spring and early summer, together with coniferous forest, is the signature of the taiga or boreal belt. Sri Lanka is equatorial and Savanna is tropical wet and dry, so neither has such winters; the Manchurian type is a cool temperate eastern margin climate with much heavier summer rain from the monsoon. Only the cold temperate continental or Siberian type fits all four clues. Matches option C.

Match the following:

| List I (Climate type) | List II (Major Area) |
|---|---|
| A. Aw | 1. Central California |
| B. Af | 2. Indian Sub Continent |
| C. Cs | 3. North and South of Amazon forests |
| D. Am | 4. Western Equatorial Africa |

Code: A B C D
solution: In Koppen's scheme Aw is the tropical wet and dry or savanna type, whose standard example regions are the Llanos of Venezuela and the Campos of Brazil, that is the belts lying north and south of the Amazon rain forest, so A goes with 3. Af is the tropical wet type of the Amazon and Congo basins, so B goes with 4, Western Equatorial Africa. Cs is the Mediterranean type with dry summers, cited for central California, so C goes with 1. Am is the tropical monsoon type quoted for the coasts of south west India, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh and Myanmar, so D goes with 2, the Indian Sub Continent. The sequence is 3, 4, 1, 2. Matches option C.

stem:
Consider the following statements:
1. Exfoliation can occur due to expansion and contraction induced by temperature changes.
2. The weathering process helps in the formation of the soil.
3. Weathering of rocks and deposits helps in the enrichment and concentrations of certain valuable ores of iron, manganese, aluminium, copper etc.
Which of the above is/are correct?
solution: Statement 1 is correct, since repeated heating and cooling makes the outer shell of a rock expand and contract differentially and peel away in curved sheets, which is exfoliation. Statement 2 is correct because weathering breaks parent rock into fine regolith, the essential first step in soil formation. Statement 3 is correct as well, for chemical weathering leaches away soluble matter and leaves residual concentrations of iron, manganese, aluminium and copper ores that are rich enough to mine. All three are therefore correct. Matches option D.

stem:
Which of the following is formed in the youthful stage of the river?
1. V shaped valley
2. Waterfalls 3. Rapids
4. Meanders
solution: In the youthful stage a river has a steep gradient and cuts downward far faster than sideways, producing a deep V shaped valley, so 1 is correct. Sharp breaks of slope and bands of hard rock in the steep upper course give waterfalls and rapids, so 2 and 3 are correct. Meanders need a gentle gradient and dominant lateral erosion on a wide floodplain, which belongs to the mature and old stages, so 4 is wrong. Only 1, 2 and 3 hold. Matches option A.

stem: Doline is formed by the:
solution: A doline, also called a sinkhole or swallow hole, is a funnel shaped hollow in limestone country. It forms where percolating groundwater charged with carbonic acid dissolves and removes the limestone along joints, so material is carried away rather than laid down. That makes it an erosional, specifically a solutional, feature of groundwater and not a work of rivers. Matches option D.

stem:
Consider the following statements:
1. Gently inclined rocky floors close to the mountains at their foot with or without a thin cover of debris, are called pediments.
2. Inselberg, which is a remnant of the mountain, is formed due to the wind erosion.
3. The playa plain covered up by salts is called alkali flats.
Which of the following statements is/are correct?
solution: Statement 1 is the standard definition of a pediment, a gently inclined rocky floor at the foot of a desert mountain front with at most a thin veneer of debris, so it is correct. Statement 2 is wrong, because an inselberg is the residual hill left as the mountain front retreats through weathering, sheet flooding and stream erosion during pediment extension, not through wind erosion. Statement 3 is correct, since a playa floor encrusted with salts left behind by evaporation is termed an alkali flat. Hence only 1 and 3 are right. Matches option C.

stem:
Consider the statements about the sand dunes:
1. Seif is similar to barchan with a small difference. Seif has two wings or points. 2. Crescent shaped dunes are called barchans.
3. Longitudinal dunes form when supply of sand is poor and wind direction is constant.
4. Transverse dunes are aligned perpendicular to wind direction.
Which of the above is/are correct?
solution: Statement 1 is wrong, because a seif resembles a barchan but keeps only ONE wing or point, not two. Statement 2 is correct, as barchans are the crescent shaped dunes with horns pointing downwind. Statement 3 is correct, since longitudinal or seif ridges develop where the sand supply is poor and the wind blows from a constant direction, giving long low ridges. Statement 4 is correct, for transverse dunes lie at right angles to the wind where sand is abundant along an elongated source. So 2, 3 and 4 are correct. Matches option B.

stem:
Which of these features is produced by wind erosion and deposition?
I. Seiff
II. Spit
III. Barchan
IV. Zeugens
Codes
solution: Seif and barchan are both sand dunes, that is features of wind deposition, so I and III qualify. Zeugen is a tabular ridge of alternating hard and soft rock sculpted by wind abrasion, so IV is a feature of wind erosion and also qualifies. A spit is a ridge of sand and shingle built out across a bay by longshore drift, which is marine and not aeolian work, so II must be excluded. The correct set is I, III and IV. Matches option D.

stem:
Consider the following:
1. The floodplains in a delta are called delta plains.
2. Natural levees are found along the banks of large rivers.
3. Meander bars are found on the concave side of meanders of large rivers and are sediments deposited in a linear fashion by flowing waters along the bank.
4. Jhelum forms meanders in its youthful stage.
How many of the above are correct?
solution: Statement 1 is correct, as the flood plains built up over a delta are termed delta plains. Statement 2 is correct, since natural levees are low ridges of coarse sediment deposited along the banks of large rivers during overbank flooding. Statement 3 is TREATED AS CORRECT here because it reproduces the NCERT wording exactly, which describes meander bars, that is point bars, as lying on the concave side of meanders and laid down in a linear fashion along the bank; note that in strict geomorphology such deposition occurs on the convex or inner bank, so the textbook wording is at odds with the physics. Statement 4 is correct, the Jhelum in the Kashmir valley being the standard Indian example of a river that meanders while still in its youthful stage. All four therefore count as correct. Matches option D.
subject: Geography
chapter: Earth's Structure, Landforms and Geological Time
reviewNote: Statement 3 is verbatim NCERT Class 11 Fundamentals of Physical Geography ch.7, which says meander bars are found on the CONCAVE side. Real geomorphology puts point-bar deposition on the CONVEX (inner) bank; the concave bank is the cut bank and erodes. Because the setter has copied NCERT word for word (as with statements 1 and 2), statement 3 is read as intended-true and the key is D (4 correct). If a marker instead grades statement 3 on physical correctness, statement 3 becomes false and the key would be C (3 correct). Source-verify against the official key before flipping.
